transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. For months now I’ve had this constant heavy, sad feeling that I just can’t seem to shake, even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy. My primary care doctor noticed how much I've changed lately and recommended I come speak with you.
How long has this sad feeling been going on, and have you had similar episodes in the past?

This heavy, sad feeling has been going on steadily for about eight months now, starting around the time my sister was diagnosed with heart problems and I took on her care. I’ve never had an episode like this in the past; this persistent sadness is entirely new to me.
Have you had any periods of normal mood lasting at least several weeks between previous episodes of sadness, or has this been your first and only episode?
This is my very first time experiencing anything like this. I've never had periods of deep sadness in the past, so this is entirely new to me.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, even when they're done with people you care about?

Yes, I've definitely lost that spark of joy. I still force myself to go to my watercolor group or walking club occasionally, but I feel like I'm just going through the motions instead of actually looking forward to them or enjoying them like I used to.
Have you also noticed a decrease in your appetite or significant weight change over these past eight months?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight over these past eight months. I seem to be eating about the same as I always do.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up frequently, or waking up much earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Yes, I have. I fall asleep easily enough, but I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my mind churning about my sister, bills, and whether I'm letting people down. I just lie there tired but completely unable to drift back to sleep.
When you wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. and can't fall back asleep, do these thoughts make you feel especially guilty, worthless, or hopeless?

Yes, that early morning hour is exactly when those feelings of guilt and worthlessness hit me the hardest. I lie there thinking that I'm failing everyone—feeling like a lousy sister for not being there in person, a poor friend for constantly canceling plans, and that I don't really bring much to anyone's life anymore.
Have you felt that life isn't worth living or had thoughts about not wanting to be here anymore during these past eight months?

I don’t have any plan to hurt myself, but on my lowest days over these last eight months, I have had those thoughts. I find myself thinking that if I just didn’t wake up one morning, it would be a relief for me and make things simpler for everyone else.
